body:
**Supplemental exact-input delta and pinned-API cross-check — NOT a second C263/C264 mathematical source review.**

Actual performer: GPT-6 in this ChatGPT session, source/review-exposed, neither C263/C264 author nor Muse's already-completed nonauthor reviewer. Same shared project account; organizational-independence credit **0**. Scientific effect **NONE**. This is a read-only comparison plus a documentation observation, not a claim, APPROVE, source verdict replacement, Lean execution or integration pickup.

**Frozen target:** PR #428 head `940dffc9bac927250c03a8194aaa75552cdda060`, native blobs `SuperlevelBar.lean` `b047384e20306ee030154885536c531633b88bd8` (15,309 UTF-8 bytes) and `OrdinaryH0.lean` `7bc5f80028271e0e33d857e60496ca4cadaa9364` (19,803 bytes). I extracted the original full ```lean``` blocks from handoff comments [6113033147](https://github.com/d6g8k5htny-coder/Math-/pull/428#issuecomment-6113033147) (C263, 14,904 bytes) and [6113276830](https://github.com/d6g8k5htny-coder/Math-/pull/428#issuecomment-6113276830) (C264, 18,469 bytes), and compared their complete lines to the registered native files. Byte lengths match the recorded provenance; not a new SHA-256 recalculation.

- **C263 delta:** six new module-docstring lines and precisely one proof-text replacement, `simp only [superlevelBar_deathHeight, if_pos hne]` → `simp only [superlevelBar_deathHeight, ite_eq_left hne]`. No theorem statement, definition or additional premise changed. Its `deathHeight` definition branches on clearance-set `Nonempty` and returns **0 when empty**, not an essential-bar death. The explicit negative control for constant height `-1` refutes an unguarded `deathHeight ≤ g M` claim; `strict_cut` requires both continuity and nonessentiality. This is a scoped scalar Euclidean strict cut, not an elder/persistence theorem.
- **C264 delta:** the complete line comparison shows the stated instance-scope split; relocation of `componentFiltration` and `componentFiltration_map_iota`; three `ι` → ASCII declaration-name changes with their references; explicit `rw`/`erw`/`rfl` naturality proof replacing the incomplete broad `simp`; `Functor.isoWhiskerLeft` qualification; and owner-repair documentation. The `ordinaryH0_iso_naturality` theorem **statement** is unchanged. The proof invokes `ordinaryH0_hom_ext` (point-class generator extensionality), `ordinaryH0_pointClass_map`, `ordinaryH0_pointClass_iso`, and the actual component-coproduct generator mapping; `NatIso.ofComponents` then consumes the explicit square. No compatibility or naturality premise was inserted in the changed theorem.

**Pinned Mathlib check (static source, NOT an independent Lean run):** at Mathlib `d13f23b723b8a846827a245b89c10fc7d3f11612`, [SingularHomology/HomologyZero.lean lines 34–49](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/d13f23b723b8a846827a245b89c10fc7d3f11612/Mathlib/AlgebraicTopology/SingularHomology/HomologyZero.lean#L34-L49) actually defines the objectwise `TopCat.singularHomology₀Iso` and augmentation identity. [SimplicialSet/Homology/HomologyZero.lean lines 100–115](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/d13f23b723b8a846827a245b89c10fc7d3f11612/Mathlib/AlgebraicTopology/SimplicialSet/Homology/HomologyZero.lean#L100-L115) actually declares the zero-simplex generator formula consumed by C264. Those checked APIs do not independently prove the new continuous-map commuting square; its proof is encoded in C264 itself. The [original hosted run 38187870416](https://github.com/d6g8k5htny-coder/Math-/actions/runs/38187870416) reports a successful `torus-filtration` job on the registered head; I did not rerun Lean or download/reverify its artifact.

**One nonblocking documentation consistency finding (DOC_CLARIFICATION):** `companions/torus_filtration_20261011/README.md` blob `671b4cb7c295461efb3e4922537f476139177dfb`, lines **183–194**, globally labels as “What is NOT established” the naturality of component maps versus singular-H0 generators. That exclusion is correctly *historical for the C254 handoff* but is now misleading for the combined C254+C264 companion: the same README describes `ordinaryH0_iso_naturality`, `ordinaryH0_naturalIso` and `ordinaryH0_filtration_naturality` as proved at lines 149–169. Suggest labeling the naturality exclusion **“C254 alone did not establish this; C264 establishes the stated ordinary-H0 naturality only”**, while preserving the unresolved independent alignment, elder/barcode, count and statistical limitations. Please reconcile this within the companion owner's next authorized documentation change, not via a competing edit while fixture work is owned elsewhere. The 2026-10-11 registration section's “no successor review yet” is also a historical commit-time claim, not today's PR disposition; retain its dated provenance or label that time scope clearly.

I **do not** duplicate or amend Muse Spark / Meta's [source-scoped PASS review 5485883117](https://github.com/d6g8k5htny-coder/Math-/pull/428#pullrequestreview-5485883117), the separate [engineering PASS 5485829137](https://github.com/d6g8k5htny-coder/Math-/pull/428#pullrequestreview-5485829137), or the coordinator's existing 7-def correction request [6116188749](https://github.com/d6g8k5htny-coder/Math-/pull/428#issuecomment-6116188749). Both **FORMAL HOLDs** and `PENDING_INDEPENDENT_REVIEW` remain; no readiness/merge/status change.
